name: Gradient boosting (GBM)
summary: Builds a strong predictor by adding small decision trees one at a time, each correcting the errors of the ones before.
inputs: Tabular feature matrix (numeric; categoricals encoded or native in histogram variants) and a target.
outputs: Point predictions (regression) or class probabilities (classification); feature importances.

data_requirements.frequency: Any; for time series build lag features and use walk-forward splits

assumptions: Rows are exchangeable (i.i.d.) unless you build time-aware features and splits
Signal is learnable from tabular features; no built-in notion of time or sequence
math_summary: Fits an additive model F(x)=sum_m nu*h_m(x) stage by stage; each new weak learner h_m (usually a small tree) is fitted to the negative gradient of the loss at the current fit, i.e. functional gradient descent.
when_to_use: Tabular data with mixed numeric and categorical features
Non-linear interactions you do not want to hand-specify
Strong baseline before trying deep models
when_not_to_use: Very small samples where a linear model is easier to defend
Pure sequence or text inputs without engineered features
When you need calibrated probabilities without post-hoc calibration
pitfalls: Leakage from random K-fold on time series: use walk-forward splits
Overfitting with deep trees and many rounds: use early stopping on a time-ordered validation set

compute.complexity: Training roughly O(n_trees * n * depth) with histogram binning; CPU-friendly, parallel across features. Inference is fast.
compute.hardware: CPU is enough for millions of rows; no GPU needed.

applicability.use_case: Credit or default-risk scoring from firm fundamentals
Nowcasting a macro series from many monthly indicators (with time-ordered splits)
